title: Attribute prefetched/prefix KV cache costs to originating microbatch/session owners
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem statement:

When prefix/KV prefetches and cache fills are performed, downstream cache hits (and the compute work that produced them) are currently billed inconsistently: sometimes charged to the filling request, sometimes to the serving microbatch, and sometimes batched away by aggregation heuristics. This leads to surprising charges for customers, incorrect quota enforcement, and confusing rate-limit behavior for high-concurrency workloads.

Goal:

Define and implement a deterministic, explainable algorithm that attributes the CPU/GPU token billing and quota consumption for prefetched/prefix/KV cache activities to the correct logical owner(s) (microbatch, user session, or origin request), while preserving latency SLOs and allowing aggregated batching to remain efficient. The algorithm must be auditable and reversible for billing reconciliation.

Scope / constraints:

- Focus on the hosted Redwood API runtime including mixed-tenant microbatch fusion paths (multi-tenant batches) and dedicated pools where per-tenant accounting matters.
- Must handle live prefix prefetches, KV cache fills, coalesced batches, and spillback flows.
- Preserve existing rate-limit semantics for synchronous requests; minimize additional tail latency.
- Keep per-request metadata delta minimal to avoid adding significant overhead to fast paths.

Proposed approach summary:

1) Distinguish three charge surfaces for a request lifecycle: generation tokens (output tokens from model), prefetch/fill compute tokens (cost to materialize KV/prefix cache entries), and aggregation/dispatch overhead (constant per-batch overhead).
2) Track a small provenance header on microbatches: origin_keys = ordered list of originating request ids (capped at 8) and origin_weights = proportional token expectations at enqueue time (integers). This header is attached only to fused microbatches and dropped for unbatched singletons.
3) When a prefetch/fill occurs as part of a microbatch, attribute the fill compute tokens to the strongest origin (highest origin_weight) unless the fill was triggered by an explicit eager prefetch API call (in which case attribute to the initiating API key).
4) For cache hits served from previously filled entries, consume zero "fill" tokens and charge only generation tokens to the serving request; however, record a light-weight provenance pointer so downstream billing reconciliation can reassign cost if the original fill is later contested.
5) For interleaved batches where multiple tenants' requests share a fill, prorate fill cost by origin_weights with a floor to the initiating origin to prevent tiny fractional charges that are noisy for billing systems.
6) Add a reconciliation job to run daily that reprocesses high-cost fills older than 24h and verifies origin attribution; inconsistencies surface as audit logs and can trigger either crediting customers or correcting invoices.

Heuristics and trade-offs noted:

- We choose origin_weight-based proration because it is simple to compute at enqueue-time and robust to reordering. Alternative (first-come-first-fill) was considered but leads to poor incentives for batching behavior.
- Caps (max 8 origin ids) keep header size small, but for extremely large fused batches we will attribute the remainder to a synthetic "batch-other" bucket owned by the pool (customers are notified).

Acceptance criteria:

- New attribution algorithm implemented in runtime metering path and feature-flagged.
- Integration tests that create synthetic interleaved multi-tenant microbatches verify that the sum of billed tokens equals compute tokens consumed within 1% tolerance.
- End-to-end tests with quota enforcement: exceeding a tenant's quota due to fills should surface throttles consistent with expected attribution rules.
- Daily reconciliation run emits zero unexpected negative-balance corrections after a 2-week pilot on a small customer cohort.

Design and implementation plan (rough):

- Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): instrument microbatch enqueue to collect origin_weights and estimate token expectations. Prototype a deterministic proration function and simulate against 7 days of historical sampling traces (see links).
- Phase 2 (implementation, 2 weeks): add provenance header to fused-batcher path, implement attribution in metering pipeline, and wire audit logs. Add feature flag.
- Phase 3 (validation, 1 week): run closed pilot (10 customers) with read-only billing reporting for detection. Launch reconciliation job in dry-run.
- Phase 4 (rollout, 1 week): enable attribution for all hosted traffic, monitor for disputes.

Observability / metrics to add:

- metric: billing.prefetch.fill.tokens.attributed.total (by origin-type: api-key | microbatch-primary | batch-other)
- metric: billing.prefetch.fill.proration.gini (distribution fairness indicator)
- metric: billing.reconcile.adjustments.count and amount
- alert if >= 0.5% of total fill tokens are unattributed (batch-other) for > 12 hours

Testing artifacts & dashboards:

- Simulation notebook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/docs/metering/prefetch-proration-sim
- Replay traces: gs://redwood-metrics/replay/prefetch-samples/2026-02
- Draft Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference.internal/d/kv-prefetch/billing-attribution

Backward compatibility and migration notes:

- For existing invoices we will not mass-correct historical charges automatically. The reconciliation job will identify candidate corrections and surface them as credits that require manual review for the first 30 days. After pilot approval we will include automatic corrections with audit trail.
- Customers that require deterministic per-request billing (enterprise) can opt-in to an alternative strict attribution mode where fills triggered by tenant-scoped prefetch API are always charged to the API key and cross-tenant fills are disallowed by policy (feature gate in Dedicated/Private).

Security & privacy:

- The provenance header contains only opaque internal request ids and coarse weights; no PII. Headers are retained per retention policy and only accessible by billing/audit roles.

Rollout plan and feature flagging:

- Default: off. Enable for 'billing-pilot' orgs by org metadata. Phase to global-on after 2 weeks of pilot with no material disputes.

Notes on rate-limits interaction:

- Rate-limit tokens consumed for a request should reflect generation tokens plus a prorated share of fill tokens if the fill was charged to that tenant. Throttling checks run using the attributed billing view to ensure enforcement consistency.

Deliverables:

- runtime change: provenance header + proration algorithm (service: fused-batcher, metering pipeline worker)
- billing pipeline change: allocation rules and reconciliation job
- e2e tests and a new Grafana dashboard
- documentation: public FAQ describing attribution rules and customer-facing examples
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation and feature-flag implemented in runtime and metering pipeline
Integration tests show billed tokens == consumed compute tokens within 1% on sample workloads
Quota enforcement behaves according to attribution rules in closed pilot
Reconciliation dry-run completes with zero high-severity disputes for pilot cohort
Public docs + FAQ published describing new attribution model
comments: 2026-02-26 — Marco Ruiz: Completed spike. Simulation shows proration by origin_weights has lower variance than first-come-first-fill across our sampled traces. See simulation notebook link in description.

2026-03-04 — Eng Review (Rafael Ortiz): Implementation note: provenance header needs to be serialized compactly (uvarint) to avoid extra allocations. We should also add a checksum to avoid malformed headers causing batch failures.
2026-03-08 — Security (Lin Wang): Reviewed header contents; confirm no PII and retention limited to 30 days. Add an ACL so only billing/audit teams can read full provenance logs.
